column1: # Every word the player reads, one row per line of text.
#   key    what the code and the .wa files name. Never change one without changing its callers.
#   where  where it shows, for whoever translates it.
#   fr     the French text. Each further column is a language, named in the header row below.
#   en     English (r162), picked with the flags on the start menu and kept in the config.
# Read by jks.index.Index_Text. Tab-separated: a tab ends a cell, so a cell cannot hold one.
# In a cell, \n is a line break. {WAVE}...{ENDWAVE}, {COLOR=...} and the like are TextraTypist
# markup - keep them around the translated word. A line starting with # is a comment.
# A text missing in a language falls back to fr; a key missing altogether shows the key itself.
# Accents: a row marked [title face] is drawn in OptimusPrinceps, which has no é è à â ç and
# no usable É (doubt d8) - write those without accents, in every language. TextTableTest checks.
# Everything else is GeosansLight and takes accents.

column1: # Ross thinks these in the bubble while the mouse is on a piece of the key.

column2: Carriage 1, thought bubble on key piece 1
column3: Je vais enfin partir d'ici! Mais où est mon bagage ?
column4: I'm finally leaving this place! But where's my bag?

column2: Carriage 1, thought bubble on key piece 2
column3: Nom de non, qui à laissé trainer tous ces cubes ?
column4: Good grief, who left all these cubes lying around?

column2: Carriage 1, thought bubble on key piece 3
column3: Ce pauvre petit oiseau a l'air affamé dans sa cage dorée. \nSi seulement je pouvais l'aider...
column4: This poor little bird looks starved in its golden cage. \nIf only I could help it...

column2: Carriage 1, cage used with sac (choice 1), bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Voilà qui devrait remplir son estomac ! \nMais s’il était {WAVE}libre{ENDWAVE}... non ?
column4: That should fill its tummy! \nBut if it were {WAVE}free{ENDWAVE}... right?

column2: Carriage 1, cage used with clefCage (choice 2), bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Libre comme l’air ! \nMais trouvera-t-il de la {WAVE}nourriture{ENDWAVE} avant de tomber dans les pommes ?
column4: Free as a bird! \nBut will it find any {WAVE}food{ENDWAVE} before it faints?

column2: Carriage 1, cage already used with sac (choice 1), then clefCage tried on it - bubble by Ross for a few seconds (r160)
column3: Il picore, tout content. \nLa cage restera fermée.
column4: It's pecking away, happy as can be. \nThe cage stays shut.

column2: Carriage 1, cage already used with clefCage (choice 2), then sac tried on it - bubble by Ross for a few seconds (r160)
column3: Il est déjà loin. \nJ'espère qu'il trouvera à manger...
column4: It's long gone. \nI hope it finds something to eat...

column1: # Ross says these when the item is clicked (r74) - edit them in the line lab:

column2: Carriage 1, cubeM.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Il manque un cube ici. Le creux a juste la bonne forme.
column4: A cube is missing here. The hollow is just the right shape.

column2: Carriage 1, cage.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Un petit oiseau tout bleu. Il me regarde comme s'il avait faim.
column4: A little blue bird. It looks at me like it's hungry.

column2: Carriage 1, clefCage.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Une toute petite clé. Elle n'ouvre sûrement pas une porte...
column4: A tiny little key. It surely doesn't open a door...

column2: Carriage 1, sac.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Des graines ! Pas pour moi, mais quelqu'un en voudra peut-être.
column4: Seeds! Not for me, but someone might want them.

column2: Carriage 1, cube.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Un cube avec un zéro dessus. Il doit bien aller quelque part.
column4: A cube with a zero on it. It must go somewhere.

column2: Carriage 1, baluchon.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Mon baluchon ! Tout ce que j'ai tient là-dedans.
column4: My bundle! Everything I own fits in there.

column1: # Ross thinks these in the bubble while the mouse is on a piece of the key.

column2: Carriage 2, thought bubble on key piece 1
column3: Je me suis toujours demandé ce qu'ils avaient écrit dans ce foutu rapport
column4: I always wondered what they wrote in that damn report

column2: Carriage 2, thought bubble on key piece 2
column3: Cette mauvaise habitude m'a toujours fait cracher mes poumons. \nJe devrais m'en débarrasser.
column4: This bad habit has always made me cough my lungs out. \nI should get rid of it.

column2: Carriage 2, thought bubble on key piece 3
column3: Le paternel a l'air presque gentil, sur ce tableau. \nIl mériterait des retouches !
column4: The old man looks almost kind in this painting. \nIt could use some touching up!

column2: Carriage 2, tableau used with crayon (choice 1), bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Des cornes, une moustache... le voilà presque drôle. \nMais il est toujours {WAVE}là{ENDWAVE}, à me juger.
column4: Horns, a moustache... he's almost funny now. \nBut he's still {WAVE}there{ENDWAVE}, judging me.

column2: Carriage 2, tableau used with couteauSocle (choice 2), bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Un coup de son propre couteau, et il ne me juge plus. \nÇa ne se {WAVE}recoud{ENDWAVE} pas...
column4: One stroke of his own knife, and he judges me no more. \nThat can't be {WAVE}sewn{ENDWAVE} back...

column2: Carriage 2, tableau already used with crayon (choice 1), then couteauSocle tried on it - bubble by Ross for a few seconds (r160)
column3: Il a déjà ses cornes et sa moustache. \nÇa lui suffira.
column4: He's got his horns and his moustache already. \nThat'll do.

column2: Carriage 2, tableau already used with couteauSocle (choice 2), then crayon tried on it - bubble by Ross for a few seconds (r160)
column3: La toile pend en lambeaux. \nPlus rien à dessiner.
column4: The canvas hangs in shreds. \nNothing left to draw on.

column1: # Ross says these when the item is clicked (r74) - edit them in the line lab:

column2: Carriage 2, tableau.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Le paternel, en uniforme. Même en peinture, il me juge.
column4: The old man, in uniform. Even in paint, he judges me.

column2: Carriage 2, clope.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Mes clopes. Une dernière, pour la route ?
column4: My smokes. One last one, for the road?

column2: Carriage 2, couteauSocle.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Le couteau de collection du vieux. « Pas touche », qu'il disait.
column4: The old man's collector knife. "Hands off", he used to say.

column2: Carriage 2, crayon.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Des crayons de couleur. De quoi égayer n'importe quelle tronche.
column4: Coloured pencils. Enough to brighten up any mug.

column2: Carriage 2, poubelle.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Une poubelle. C'est là que finissent les mauvaises habitudes.
column4: A bin. That's where bad habits end up.

column2: Carriage 2, dossierPolice.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Mon dossier de police. Ils ont écrit un roman sur moi, on dirait.
column4: My police file. Looks like they wrote a novel about me.

column1: # Ross thinks these in the bubble while the mouse is on a piece of the key.

column2: Carriage 3, thought bubble on key piece 1
column3: Si les gens savaient ce qui s'est passé ici... \nJe dois écrire tout ce que j'ai vu.
column4: If only people knew what happened here... \nI have to write down everything I saw.

column2: Carriage 3, thought bubble on key piece 2
column3: Ma douce Diana me manques, je devrais vraiment lui envoyer un signe de vie
column4: I miss my sweet Diana, I really should send her a sign of life

column2: Carriage 3, thought bubble on key piece 3
column3: Le trou dans ce mur semble bien étrange. Je pourrais le fixer… ou le finir.
column4: That hole in the wall looks very strange. I could fix it… or finish it.

column2: Carriage 3, trou used with porteTrou (choice 1), bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Voilà, le mur tient. Plus rien à voir dehors. \nComme si tout se {WAVE}refermait{ENDWAVE} si vite...
column4: There, the wall holds. Nothing more to see outside. \nAs if everything could {WAVE}close up{ENDWAVE} that fast...

column2: Carriage 3, trou used with grenade (choice 2), bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Plus de mur du tout. On voit {WAVE}dehors{ENDWAVE}, maintenant. \nPourvu que personne n'ait été derrière...
column4: No more wall at all. You can see {WAVE}outside{ENDWAVE} now. \nI just hope nobody was behind it...

column2: Carriage 3, trou already used with porteTrou (choice 1), then grenade tried on it - bubble by Ross for a few seconds (r160)
column3: Le mur tient. \nJe ne vais pas tout défaire.
column4: The wall holds. \nI'm not undoing all of it.

column2: Carriage 3, trou already used with grenade (choice 2), then porteTrou tried on it - bubble by Ross for a few seconds (r160)
column3: Plus de mur à boucher. \nIl ne reste que dehors.
column4: No wall left to patch. \nThere's only outside now.

column1: # Ross says these when the item is clicked (r74) - edit them in the line lab:

column2: Carriage 3, trou.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Un trou dans le mur. Quelque chose est passé par là.
column4: A hole in the wall. Something came through here.

column2: Carriage 3, porteTrou.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Un morceau de mur. Il a à peu près la forme du trou.
column4: A piece of wall. It's roughly the shape of the hole.

column2: Carriage 3, grenade.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Une grenade. Mieux vaut la tenir loin de moi.
column4: A grenade. Best kept well away from me.

column2: Carriage 3, lettreAmour.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Une lettre pour Diana. Je ne l'ai jamais envoyée.
column4: A letter for Diana. I never sent it.

column2: Carriage 3, appareil.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Mon appareil photo. Il a vu plus de choses que moi.
column4: My camera. It has seen more than I have.

column2: Carriage 3, chapeau.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Mon vieux chapeau. Il a connu des jours meilleurs.
column4: My old hat. It has seen better days.

column2: Carriage 3, boite.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Une boîte aux lettres. Il paraît que le courrier passe encore.
column4: A mailbox. They say the post still gets through.

column1: # Ross thinks these in the bubble while the mouse is on a piece of the key.

column2: Carriage 4, thought bubble on key piece 1
column3: Ca fait changement de prendre des photos de la vie plutôt que la mort
column4: Makes a change, taking pictures of life rather than death

column2: Carriage 4, thought bubble on key piece 2
column3: Il est tellement jolie le hochet. Il manque quelque chose par contre ...
column4: The rattle is so pretty. Something's missing though ...

column2: Carriage 4, thought bubble on key piece 3
column3: J'ai la gorge sèche et le coeur qui s'agite. Je devrais boire quelque chose avant de partir...
column4: My throat is dry and my heart is racing. I should drink something before I leave...

column2: Carriage 4, verre used with cruche (choice 1), bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: De l'eau fraîche. Les idées claires, les mains qui tremblent. \nIl faudra bien {WAVE}rester{ENDWAVE} debout...
column4: Fresh water. A clear head, shaking hands. \nI'll have to {WAVE}stay{ENDWAVE} on my feet...

column2: Carriage 4, verre used with wisky (choice 2), bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Une gorgée, et la gare paraît moins loin. \nCette bouteille a un goût de {WAVE}départ{ENDWAVE}...
column4: One sip, and the station seems closer. \nThis bottle tastes of {WAVE}leaving{ENDWAVE}...

column2: Carriage 4, verre already used with cruche (choice 1), then wisky tried on it - bubble by Ross for a few seconds (r160)
column3: J'ai choisi l'eau. \nJe la bois jusqu'au bout.
column4: I chose the water. \nI'll drink it to the last drop.

column2: Carriage 4, verre already used with wisky (choice 2), then cruche tried on it - bubble by Ross for a few seconds (r160)
column3: Trop tard pour l'eau. \nLe whisky me brûle déjà la gorge.
column4: Too late for water. \nThe whisky's already burning my throat.

column1: # Ross says these when the item is clicked (r74) - edit them in the line lab:

column2: Carriage 4, cadre.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Ma femme, et le bébé qui arrive. Le plus beau portrait que j'ai fait.
column4: My wife, and the baby on the way. The best portrait I ever took.

column2: Carriage 4, cruche.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Une cruche d'eau fraîche. Rien de plus simple.
column4: A jug of fresh water. Nothing simpler.

column2: Carriage 4, hochet.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Le hochet du petit. Il a l'air un peu nu.
column4: The little one's rattle. It looks a bit bare.

column2: Carriage 4, verre.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Un verre vide. Il attend que je décide quoi y verser.
column4: An empty glass. It's waiting for me to decide what to pour.

column2: Carriage 4, wisky.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Une bouteille de whisky. Une vieille amie... de trop.
column4: A bottle of whisky. An old friend... one too many.

column2: Carriage 4, papier.png clicked, bubble by Ross for a few seconds
column3: Du papier cadeau et un ruban. De quoi emballer quelque chose de joli.
column4: Wrapping paper and a ribbon. Enough to wrap something pretty.
